companions.name: OGLE-LMC-ECL-10567 B
companions.description: The secondary star of the eclipsing binary OGLE-LMC-ECL-10567, 3.184 solar masses and 36.64 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 117.975 days.

radius.source: Secondary radius (solar radii) 36.64 +/- 0.25, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)

mass.source: Secondary mass (solar masses) 3.184 +/- 0.026, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)

temperature.source: Secondary log Teff 3.673 +/- 0.007, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G): 4710 K

orbit.source: OGLE-LMC-ECL-10567: P 117.9747 d and primary-eclipse time HJD 2452168.4 (arXiv:1805.04952, Table 1 (tbl:1), column $T_0$ (HJD-2450000) and table comment); i 83.7 degrees (arXiv:1805.04952, Table 6, column $i$ (deg)); e 0 (circular). HJD is taken as BJD_TDB (under a minute apart); at the primary eclipse the secondary is in front, the component these papers call primary being the one eclipsed at phase 0. Separation from Kepler's third law with DEBCat's masses

text.card: The secondary star of OGLE-LMC-ECL-10567, a pair that eclipse each other every 117.975 days.
text.introduction: It has 3.184 solar masses and 36.64 solar radii; its partner has 3.333 and 24.6, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), OGLE-LMC-ECL-10567: Mass, Radius and Period, from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)
